scope: Evidence reference for generally healthy adults; requires the separate safety policy before use.
reference_assumptions: Adult age 18 or older, not pregnant or breastfeeding.
No relevant medical conditions, medicines, other supplements, or other caffeine intake.
Strength means regular resistance or repeated high-intensity training.
Any caffeine serving is taken in the morning, at least 8 hours before bedtime.
Balls are dose units in a reference model, not instructions to weigh pure caffeine or manufacture food.
A single day's visualization does not establish a supplement's immediate benefit.

decision.reference_automatic_qualification: Only under every visible reference assumption and all goal-specific vetoes. Unknown or failed assumptions mean withhold rather than infer safety. Energy denotes acute alertness only, not correction of unexplained fatigue or all-day energy.
decision.important_overlap_limit: Creatine has uncertain population-dependent memory findings. L-theanine has limited sleep and stress signals. Neither overlap earns automatic goal coverage.

model_policy.minimum_effective_dose: Do not count a benefit below its tested or defensible serving threshold.
model_policy.dose_response: Do not imply that more balls produce proportionally more benefit or guarantee an outcome.
model_policy.utility_scores: Any optimizer weights are transparent design heuristics, not percentages of efficacy, health, or goal achievement.
model_policy.abstention: A zero-ball plan is valid, including when all prioritized goals lack an eligible candidate.
model_policy.combination: Evidence for individual ingredients does not validate a combined supplement stack.
model_policy.goal_coverage: Covered means an eligible candidate has a relevant supported claim and reaches its reference dose; it does not mean the goal will be achieved.
model_policy.energy_goal: Acute alertness; not metabolic energy, persistent fatigue treatment, or an all-day productivity promise.

candidates.name: Creatine monohydrate

required: Strength prioritized with regular resistance or repeated high-intensity exercise
exclusions: Attempt to show an acute same-day strength benefit

dose.frequency: Daily, including rest days; no loading phase
dose.time_horizon: Approximately 3 to 4 weeks of daily use before muscle stores and training effects should be expected

benefits.population: Adults performing repeated high-intensity activity or resistance training
benefits.claim: Supports high-intensity exercise capacity and training adaptations over time.

benefits.population: Signals in older or stressed populations; not a reliable general healthy-adult claim
benefits.claim: Potential overlap remains uncertain and does not establish memory benefit at this 3 g reference dose.

limitations: Memory results and doses cannot be carried across populations
Memory may be annotated as emerging when already selected for Strength, but does not earn goal coverage or select creatine alone.

candidates.name: Caffeine

required: Focus or Energy prioritized; Energy means acute alertness
Morning serving at least 8 hours before bedtime
exclusions: Pure or concentrated caffeine powder preparation

quantity_per_ball.note: Reference unit only; 25 mg alone does not receive the 75 mg serving claim.

dose.frequency: Single morning serving in this model; the three units represent one serving
dose.time_horizon: Acute alertness/attention; trial testing approximately 30 minutes after a serving

benefits.population: Generally healthy adult caffeine users and nonusers
benefits.claim: Can improve acute alertness and some attention/reaction-time measures.
Can improve alertness and reduce perceived mental fatigue acutely; not a treatment for persistent fatigue.

limitations: Not a memory supplement in this model
75 mg is not a supported strength-performance dose
May impair sleep or increase restlessness
Safety reference ceilings are not intake targets or personal guarantees
8-hour timing rule is a conservative planner assumption; it does not guarantee unaffected sleep

candidates.name: L-theanine

required: A single timed serving for an acute attention task
exclusions: Claim of generalized calm, stress resilience, or sustained productivity

dose.frequency: One dose 30 to 60 minutes before cognitive testing; do not infer chronic daily efficacy or safety

benefits.population: Healthy adults in acute cognitive-testing trials
benefits.claim: A 200 mg single dose improved choice reaction-time measures in a recent synthesis; sustained everyday productivity was not established.

benefits.population: Healthy and clinical populations with stress-related outcomes
benefits.claim: Acute stress reduction was modest and driven substantially by high-risk-of-bias studies; anxiety results were inconsistent.

benefits.population: Mixed ages and health status; many products combined ingredients
benefits.claim: Subjective sleep signals do not establish an effective pure-L-theanine sleep dose or objective sleep improvement.

limitations: No established official tolerable upper limit located
No serious events reported in included short trials does not establish broad safety
2026 review COI: Guillaume Fond founded a company selling dietary supplements

candidates.name: Magnesium

required: Established nutritional or clinical indication outside this planner
exclusions: Routine sleep or calm recommendation in generally healthy adults
Selecting an arbitrary nutritional dose as an effective sleep dose

quantity_per_ball.note: Illustrative unit only; not an established effective sleep dose and never automatically selected.

dose.frequency: No effective routine sleep dose established for this population

benefits.population: Adults with heterogeneous sleep complaints; older-adult trials do not establish benefit for all healthy adults
benefits.claim: Findings are inconsistent and do not support routine magnesium use for insomnia.

limitations: Elemental magnesium must not be confused with total salt weight
Correcting deficiency is a different indication from improving a goal in a nondeficient adult

candidates.name: Protein

required: Known total dietary intake and a protein gap
Count food protein and check product allergens
exclusions: Using an identical fixed supplement dose for everyone

quantity_per_ball.note: Nutrient quantity, not powder mass; research-only illustration.

dose.frequency: Fill an assessed food-dependent gap; not a universal 20 g/day supplement prescription

benefits.population: Healthy adults undertaking prolonged resistance training
benefits.claim: Supplementation can modestly augment training gains; total protein intake matters more than adding a universal serving.

limitations: An approximate 1.6 g/kg/day plateau for fat-free-mass gain is a population estimate, not a universal minimum requirement or personal prescription

candidates.name: Glycine

exclusions: Routine sleep, focus, or resilience recommendation

dose.frequency: Studies used 3 g before bedtime over very short periods; not a validated planner prescription

benefits.claim: Early sleep findings have insufficient quality for automatic selection.

limitations: An amount used in a study is not automatically an effective or recommended dose

candidates.name: Melatonin

exclusions: Unspecified timing in a one-screen day plan

quantity_per_ball.note: No ball dose assigned because indication and timing are absent.

benefits.population: Some jet-lag or shift-related sleep problems; not all healthy-adult sleep priorities
benefits.claim: Possible usefulness for selected circadian problems does not justify routine automatic sleep planning.

limitations: Guidelines cited by NCCIH advise against use for chronic insomnia

sources.title: NIH ODS: Dietary Supplements for Exercise and Athletic Performance
sources.verified: Relevant creatine efficacy, monohydrate form, no-loading 3–6 g/day protocol and 3–4-week duration.

sources.title: EFSA: Caffeine and increased alertness (2014)
sources.verified: Reiterates 75 mg serving threshold; most outcomes below 75 mg were null. Scientific substantiation is not a claim of EU marketing authorization.

sources.title: Haskell et al.: Cognitive and mood improvements of caffeine in habitual consumers and habitual non-consumers
sources.verified: 48 adults; 75 or 150 mg drink; acute attention/alertness measures 30 minutes after intake.

sources.title: EFSA: Caffeine safety
sources.verified: Healthy nonpregnant adult references: 200 mg single intake and 400 mg daily from all sources; even 100 mg near bedtime can affect sleep.

sources.title: Prokopidis et al.: Effects of creatine supplementation on memory in healthy individuals
sources.verified: Older-adult subgroup signal; younger subgroup null. Later methodological criticism means pooled cognition findings should not stand alone.

sources.title: EFSA: Creatine and improvement in cognitive function
sources.verified: A general cause-and-effect cognition claim was not established.

sources.title: Citherlet: Commentary on the effects of creatine supplementation on cognitive function
sources.verified: Raises double-counting/nonindependent-outcome concerns in cognition meta-analysis; record used as a reason for caution, not efficacy evidence.

sources.title: Gerolymos et al.: Cognitive and affective effects of L-Theanine: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 31 randomized trials
sources.verified: 31 trials, 1168 total participants; acute 200 mg attention signal; stress high-bias, anxiety inconsistent, no fatigue effect. Full publisher article unavailable; PubMed abstract and conflict statement inspected.
sources.conflicts_of_interest: Guillaume Fond founded a company selling dietary supplements.

sources.title: Bulman et al.: The effects of L-theanine consumption on sleep outcomes
sources.verified: 19 articles, 897 participants; subjective but no objective sleep benefit; many combined ingredients, adequate pure-theanine dose unresolved.

sources.title: Lopresti et al.: Magnesium Supplementation for Sleep in Adults
sources.verified: 12 main sleep RCTs; heterogeneous outcomes and formulations, low to very low certainty; routine insomnia use unsupported.

sources.title: Mah and Pitre: Oral magnesium supplementation for insomnia in older adults
sources.verified: Three trials, 151 older adults, moderate-to-high bias and low/very-low certainty; not a general healthy-adult dose recommendation.

sources.title: Morton et al.: Protein supplementation and resistance-training gains in healthy adults
sources.verified: 49 studies, 1863 participants; modest extra training gains and an approximate 1.6 g/kg/day total-intake plateau for fat-free-mass gain.

sources.title: The effect of glycine administration on physiological systems in human adults
sources.verified: 3 g bedtime sleep studies were short, small and high risk of bias.

sources.title: NCCIH: Sleep Disorders and Complementary Health Approaches
sources.verified: Melatonin usefulness is indication-dependent; chronic-insomnia guidelines advise against it; short-term versus long-term safety differs.
